title: Global mean sea level curves
note: Two published curves: the long-term Phanerozoic tectono-glacio-eustatic curve of van der Meer et al. (2022), 1 Myr from 0 to 540 Ma with min/max, from the supplementary table of a CC BY 4.0 article; and the Late Pleistocene sea-level stack of Spratt & Lisiecki (2016), 0-798 ka at 1 kyr, from NOAA (CC BY 3.0 per the NOAA landing page). Neither is a measurement: the first is a model driven by strontium isotopes and ice estimates, the second a principal component of seven proxy records. The Haq family of short-term curves is journal copyright and not used.
cite: van der Meer, D. G., Scotese, C. R., Mills, B. J. W., Sluijs, A., van den Berg van Saparoea, A.-P., & van de Weg, R. M. B. (2022). Long-term Phanerozoic global mean sea level: Insights from strontium isotope variations and estimates of continental glaciation. Gondwana Research, 111, 103-121. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gr.2022.07.014 (CC BY 4.0)

Spratt, R. M., & Lisiecki, L. E. (2016). A Late Pleistocene sea level stack. Climate of the Past, 12, 1079-1092. https://doi.org/10.5194/cp-12-1079-2016. Data: NOAA/WDS Paleoclimatology, https://doi.org/10.25921/RD66-5820 (CC BY 3.0)
